summary: This bill lowers from 16 to 14 the age at which minors in the District of Columbia can be excluded from Family Court jurisdiction and transferred to adult criminal proceedings for certain offenses by amending sections 16-2301 and 16-2307 of the D.C. Official Code, applying to crimes committed after enactment.

scores.thoughts: The bill makes no reference to government budgets, appropriations, or spending levels of any kind. It solely amends age thresholds in the DC criminal code.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
The legislation contains nothing related to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No mention of firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not touch on immigration, border policy, or noncitizen status.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions concerning military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
The bill has zero connection to environmental regulations or climate policy.
No references to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety-net benefits.
The legislation does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

The bill directly lowers the age (from 16 to 14) at which minors in the District of Columbia can be tried as adults for certain offenses and transferred out of family court. This change expands the reach of the adult criminal justice system to younger juveniles, which aligns with a 'tougher sentencing' approach rather than emphasizing juvenile rehabilitation.
No content related to trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The legislation contains nothing about foreign aid or international assistance.
No references to voting rights, election procedures, or voter ID.
The bill does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No content related to labor law, unions, or worker protections.
The bill makes no mention of religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination law.
